title: Speed up landed CI repeat checks

intentCoverage.report:
# Dough Intent Coverage: SEED-314#speed-up-landed-ci-repeat-checks

**Verdict: Caught.** Limited to the paths observed below.

## What was checked

- **Story and revision.** SEED-314#speed-up-landed-ci-repeat-checks at `442e7c284e0683dbaf8acc7eccdfb06bdc2317fb` (branch `claude/speed-up-landed-ci-repeat-checks`), plan `.planning/slice-plans/595-speed-up-landed-ci-repeat-checks/PLAN.md`.
- **Promise.** Key example "The original stays": "Each outcome keeps the original 120 s and the 100 s average beside it", for outcomes that are now read from saved accepted requests instead of journeys. Expected observable: after collection decides a saved request's outcome, the request still names attempt 1 with its 120 s wall time and the 100 s average.
- **Fault.** Collection replaces a request's original with the measured repeat when it saves the outcome. `dashboard/server/ciFollowUpCollection.ts`, in `collectCiFollowUps`' observation loop: `: { ...current, outcome },` became `: { ...current, outcome, original: outcome.repeat ?? current.original },`. One product edit; fixtures and assertions untouched. The plan's F1–F11 do not exercise this promise with a product fault; slice 4 showed only a test-side scratch (`originalMs: 121000`).

## Consequential revision of the suggested target

The suggested fault (dropping the `admitted.request !== undefined` guard, to be caught by `expect(rerunRequests(github)).toEqual([])` in the saved-request cases) was not used. By reading the selected revision, that edit cannot go wrong on the saved-request path: `saveRepeatRequests` writes the ledger with `projects: {}`, so `hasRepeatAuthority` is false and `collectCiFollowUps` returns before the sending loop; that machine also keeps no landed history, so `keptLandingReferences(history)` would yield nothing. With or without the guard the provider receives no rerun request there, so a green run would have established nothing about the assertion. This is reading, not a faulted observation: no verdict is claimed for the `toEqual([])` count in the two saved-request cases. Exactly-once remains carried by the journeys (plan F2: lifecycle and refused). The focused command and the maintained checks are the suggested ones, unchanged.

## Evidence

Scratch checkout: `git worktree add --detach /Users/terryyin/.claude/jobs/7b8897aa/tmp/intent-coverage 442e7c284…`, `/opt/homebrew/bin` first on PATH, Node 24.21.0; `node scripts/setup-native.mjs npm`, `browser`, `check` each exited 0. Pre-probe state: `git status --porcelain` empty at `442e7c284`.

Command, from the scratch root, for baseline, fault and restored runs alike:
`caffeinate -s -i env -u NO_COLOR -u FORCE_COLOR -u GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES npm run --silent test:dashboard -- backend-tests/intent/landed-ci-automatic-repeat.spec.ts backend-tests/intent/landed-ci-repeat-verdict.spec.ts --workers=1 --reporter=list`

| Run | One-minute load before → after | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Baseline | 20.2 → 16.5 | exit 0, 5 passed (36.0 s) |
| Scratch witness, fault applied | 16.3 → (not sampled) | exit 0, 1 passed (7.8 s) |
| Fault applied | (after witness) → 27.6 | exit 1, 3 failed, 2 passed (35.2 s) |
| Restored | 24.5 → 38.9 | exit 0, 5 passed (34.9 s) |

No run needed narrowing or a wait; no journey reached its 30 s bound (slowest 12.1 s).

- **Reach and wrong behavior, observed independently.** A temporary untracked spec (`dashboard/backend-tests/intent/zz-intent-coverage-witness.spec.ts`, no assertion on the original) saved one accepted request for run 71 (120 s against 100 s) through `saveRepeatRequests`, set a 104 s repeat, started a real collecting server, waited for outcome `recovered`, and printed the saved request. With the fault it printed `original.runAttempt: 2`, `startedAt 2026-11-10T07:00:00.000Z`, `completedAt 2026-11-10T07:01:44.000Z` (104 s), `averageMs: 100000`, outcome `recovered`: the saved original was replaced by the repeat on the saved-request path.
- **Maintained assertions that caught it.**
  - `landed-ci-automatic-repeat.spec.ts:207`, in "saved accepted requests read the outcome their provider repeat decides beside the original and average": `expect(savedRepeatComparison(server, run)).toEqual({ run, attempt: 1, originalMs: 120000, averageMs: 100000 })` failed for run 71 with received `attempt: 2`, `originalMs: 104000`. This is the catch on the selected promise's path (recovered saved request).
  - Also failed, on the journeys: the lifecycle case at `:78` (card `originalMs` 106000 instead of 105000, 5 s poll) and the uncertain journey at `:138` (card `originalMs` 104000 instead of 120000).
- **Passed under the fault.** The refused journey (no measured repeat, so the fault does nothing there) and the verdict spec's saved-request case. In that case the comparison (`:57`-area loop) runs before the absent and null conclusions turn to success; whether the original was replaced after that transition was not independently observed, so nothing is claimed about that path. Likewise the failed, cancelled and partial saved requests carry no measured repeat, so this fault does not reach them; the catch is for the recovered request only.
- **Restoration.** `git checkout -- dashboard/server/ciFollowUpCollection.ts`, witness spec deleted; `git status --porcelain` empty and `git diff --stat HEAD` empty at `442e7c284`, matching the pre-probe state; the same command then passed 5 of 5. The scratch worktree was removed afterwards (`git worktree remove --force`); the execution checkout was not edited and stays clean. No commits. Logs: `/Users/terryyin/.claude/jobs/7b8897aa/tmp/ic-baseline.log`, `ic-witness-fault.log`, `ic-fault.log`, `ic-restored.log`.

## Next proof action

None required for the selected promise on the observed path: the maintained comparison at `landed-ci-automatic-repeat.spec.ts:207` catches a replaced original for the recovered saved request, and two journeys catch it on the card.

Open observations the evidence supports gathering, should the caller want them (not verdicts): (1) a faulted observation that makes a saved accepted request's machine send a rerun request, since the suggested guard edit cannot reach `rerunRequests(github)` `toEqual([])` there; (2) whether the verdict case would notice the original changing after an absent or null conclusion turns to success.

## Prior dispositions matched

- Plan slice 4, refactor pass: "a scratch `originalMs: 121000` fails the comparison". This probe adds a product-side fault failing the same comparison; it is recognition of that existing proof, not a new repair decision.
- Plan proof-ownership row "Exactly once …: the saved-request cases expect no rerun request" and F2's owners (lifecycle, refused journey) are consistent with the reading above. No new repair decision arises from this probe.

## Cost

- **Test runtime.** 113.9 s (measured), sum of the Playwright-reported durations of the four runs: 36.0 + 7.8 + 35.2 + 34.9 s. Whole-command wall time per run was not separately timed.
- **Human effort.** Unavailable. No human took part in this invocation and no measure was recorded.
- **Agent effort.** 10 tool-call rounds by one agent (measured, counted from this invocation up to the report finisher); token usage unavailable, as the agent cannot read its own meter.


- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 221277 ms (measured), from 1794456147751 to 1794456369028 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

---

## Wrap-up disposition

- Checked revision: `442e7c284e0683dbaf8acc7eccdfb06bdc2317fb`.
- Verdict received: Caught, for the recovered saved request's original and average, with the lifecycle and uncertain journeys catching the same fault on the card.
- Decision: no follow-up. The probe found no assertion gap and no missing test path on the selected promise.
- Open observations named by the report, kept as stated and not verdicts: the saved-request cases' expectation of no rerun request cannot be reached by the send-guard fault, because a machine holding only saved requests has no repeat authority, so exactly once stays proved by the lifecycle and refused journeys (plan fault F2); and the verdict case reads the original before the absent and null conclusions turn to success.
- Canonical follow-up links: none.
